Select ASVs Using Random Forest

Source: R/RandomForest_selected_ASVs.R
RandomForest_selected_ASVs.Rd

This function selects the most important ASVs (Amplicon Sequence Variants) based on a Random Forest model. The selected ASVs are saved to a CSV file.

RandomForest_selected_ASVs(
  physeq,
  response_var,
  minlib = 15000,
  prunescale = 1e-04,
  ntree = 100,
  n_top_predictors = 50,
  output_csv = "randomforest_results.csv",
  na_vars = NULL
)

Arguments

physeq

A phyloseq object containing the microbiome data.

response_var

A character string specifying the response variable from the sample data.

minlib

A numeric value specifying the minimum library size. Default is 15000.

prunescale

A numeric value specifying the pruning scale for rare OTUs. Default is 0.0001.

ntree

An integer specifying the number of trees to grow in the Random Forest. Default is 100.

n_top_predictors

An integer specifying the number of top predictors to select. Default is 50.

output_csv

A character string specifying the output CSV file name. Default is "randomforest_results.csv".

na_vars

A character vector specifying the sample data variables to check for NA values. Default is NULL.

Value

A pruned phyloseq object containing the selected ASVs.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  # Ensure you have a phyloseq object `physeq`
  # Use the name of the column in sample_data for response_var
  rf_physeq <- RandomForest_selected_ASVs(physeq_16SOTU, response_var = "Host.genus",
    na_vars = c("Habitat", "Ecoregion.III", "Host.genus", "Diet"))
}
